identity: Neutral nitrate radical NO3, CAS 12033-49-7, associated with the X2A2-prime electronic state; not nitrate anionNO3-. ATcT calls this formula ON(O)O nitroxyl, which must not be confused with neutral HNO.
recommendation: Evaluate a retained-thermal ATcT energy-only candidate, while keeping full thermal replacement as a distinct vibronic-state follow-up. Near-exact NASA/JANAF agreement is shared-source consistency, not independent proof of thermal accuracy.
science: NASA explicitly cites Chase 1998 for NO3; native NASA/JANAF atomization energy differs by only 1.286 J/mol and their aligned K ratio is within 0.021% of unity. ATcT reduces physical atomization energy by 1.917 kJ/mol, giving a retained-thermal K ratio 0.858 at 1500 K and 0.944 at 4000 K. That bounded energy direction is accessible even though complete vibronic thermochemistry remains unresolved.
modern: Larsson and Viel 2024 was inspected in full. Its coupled five-electronic-state potential and roughly 2500 vibronic eigenstates establish substantial nonadiabatic effects and assignments through roughly 6000 cm-1; the authors note possible missing states above 5800 cm-1. This is not a complete rotational/vibronic partition function over 1500-4000 K. It gives a concrete source for a future thermal study, not permission to splice 2500 vibrational levels into a complete molecular Q without rotation, spin and convergence work.
importance: NO3 is an atmospheric oxidant in nighttime chemistry. Its tiny abundance in the present hot H-rich equilibrium grid cannot validate an illuminated or nocturnal oxidizing chemical network.
conventions: Use the neutral radical CAS and doublet manifold, not the stable nitrate anion. Coupled electronic surfaces must not be counted once as vibronic states and again as an independent electronic partition factor. Atomic balances and conventional evaluated entropy are retained; no extra nuclear-spin or symmetry multiplier is added to the existing source functions.
followup: Construct a physical ATcT-minus-JANAF energy shift with fixed inherited thermal function and fit residual; validate and run current-network substitutions. A new thermal candidate needs coupled vibronic levels, rotational treatment and high-energy completeness beyond the 2024 finite spectrum. The 2024 DOI is available; no extra paper is mandatory for the bounded energy candidate or review merge.
